thread.title: Micron Headed To The 20s? - Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU)

author: Elazar Advisors, LLC
title: Micron Headed To The 20s? - Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU)
text:
Micron (NASDAQ: MU ) had a very rough guide on Wednesday. The guide down was way below the Street. People caught up in the low valuation story I think are ignoring earnings. As earnings drop, stocks drop. I think Micron can hit into the 20s.
Demand Slowing Here's what we said in our recent note Dec. 6 ahead of Micron earnings.
"Micron is going to have to make some downward adjustments vs. their previous internal outlook."
Previously on Nov. 21 we pointed out that Micron's pricing assumptions were going to have to drop.
We said then,
"Micron tried not to, but I think they ended up giving a lot of information on their last earnings call. Backing into gross margins and capex tells you pricing is expected to come down more meaningfully. They need demand to pick up, but it's slowing. They need that demand because their capex plans are going to run faster than revenue growth, making for EPS and margin deleverage risk."
In fact their demand did slow strong enough to now force Micron to have to stall their capex plans.
Here's what Micron said on Wednesday's earnings ,
"Turning to our DRAM industry outlook, as I've mentioned previously, DRAM demand weakened through the course of our fiscal first quarter. Since the start of this fiscal second quarter, the weakening demand trend has continued and our near-term visibility is limited."
That accounts for four months of slowing but they expect that to continue in 2019.
The issue is they saw the same slowing demand trend in the previous quarter reported in September.
This is how Micron described that quarter at a recent conference .
"And we saw that overall demand also and the market - overall market environment weakened through the course of the quarter."
So add it up and you have demand slowing for more than half of a year.
I would argue that Micron was blindsided to some degree by this slowdown given they were buying stock at much higher prices.
I know they also said they expect a pickup in the second half of 2019 but there's no way to know. The same way they were surprised by this demand slowdown, they can continue to be surprised by it.
We've had a strong multi-year up-cycle. It's very normal that this can be longer than two-three quarters back down.
We also saw in calendar Q3 2018 many large tech companies reported a slowdown (Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN ), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), Facebook (NASDAQ: FB )). We can't be sure that the slowdown is simply an inventory correction as Micron posits.
Thanks to the trade war negotiations we'd guess CEOs are waiting to make big decisions until there's a resolution. So it makes sense you have a slowing now along with the next 90 day US-China negotiating period.
That slowing trend can continue to hit numbers and spook investors.
Do trends pick back up if the trade war's resolved? My guess is that a downcycle was triggered already by trade negotiation uncertainty. So trade resolution would be a market positive when/if announced but may not reignite growth rates until a normal downcycle works its way out fully.
In the meantime there's more compounding uncertainty.
Big Guide Down They guided earnings for next quarter to $1.75 vs. the street at the time at $2.50. That's a big miss. They guided revenues to $5.7B which is a big drop from the recent quarter of $7.9B.
This downward trajectory we've been predicting based on dropping memory prices is risk to future quarters also dropping.
The added issue this time though was not just pricing. Pricing did drop in DRAM to -9% vs. flat in the previous quarter. However in addition to pricing there's a large drop in volume growth too - they call bit growth. Based on demand slowing Micron had to pull back on capacity to avoid risking profits further.
Here's what they said about bit growth on Wednesday.
"Due to the weaker demand environment, we expect fiscal second quarter sequential bit shipments to be down meaningfully for both NAND and DRAM."
So you not only have a drop in pricing but you also have a drop now in the other driver to revenues, bit growth (volumes).
Modeling this out starts to get us much lower earnings in forward quarters even if bit growth starts picking up.
7th Inning Stretch Side Note On Earnings Models We don't buy stocks because they are cheap. If they are cheap, great. Instead we focus on building an income statement and mapping out a realistic trajectory of where revenues, margins, expenses and EPS are going. We base that on what had been the trends and what's going on now. Then we slap a midpoint historical PE on our EPS number. If we have 45% upside it qualifies for a buy.
We don't think it makes sense to have opinions on stocks without understanding how the earnings model is playing out. That earnings model is being used by many if not most of the largest funds to decide where stocks should trade.
Liking a stock because it's going up is good until it stops going up. Then you have to be disciplined to decide it stopped going up.
Liking a stock on valuation alone also doesn't help much because stocks go up and down on low valuations.
But focusing on where the earnings are going, up or down, that's the data that drives us to want to buy or sell. We strongly believe that's what drives the biggest players to want to buy or sell.
You've seen when companies report earnings, stocks move up or down 10%. That's because the large market players readjust their forward quarters to define the valuation.
Earnings days are such glaring proof that earnings matter most for stocks, so why not focus on earnings?
So having an opinion based on the stock going up works as long as it goes up.
But having an opinion based on the earnings helps you stay disciplined to enter or exit. As that earnings trajectory changes you have the discipline to hold on or exit. No emotion, just letting the data define your direction.
For Micron we exited in the high 40s in September when we saw this slowdown happening. This slowdown continues and gets worse so there's no reason to step up, for us anyway.
Guide Down Means Lower Future Quarters Too Let's turn some of Micron's words into numbers.

You can see that if bit growth and ASP growth continue to drop you have revenues that fall off pretty meaningfully.
Scroll down to the bottom of the grid above and you see what our EPS numbers turn out to be much lower vs. the Street estimates. Those Street estimates were prior to earnings on Wednesday.
If trends don't change, which Micron hopes they will but can't know, then EPS gets below $1 per quarter.
Mid-20s? What PE has Micron traded at? What PE should it trade at? Right or wrong we keep our process pretty consistent. We try to use the midpoint historical PE and multiply that to our year-out earnings number.
Our earnings number for 2019 drops to a little over $4 (See full model: Pay Wall ), taking some of these trends, the company's commentary, and our own guestimates.
Here's the PE range the stock has traded in.
Zacks
We exclude the part where the PE went nuts as an outlier. Most of that straight line in the last three years the PE ranged from 3-9. The midpoint would be 6.
6x our 2019 of $4.00 = $24.
In the comments section on Dec. 7 in our Micron earnings preview which predicted weakness we said the following,
"Valuation stayed low when fundamentals were moving up. Now fundamentals are moving down, you think valuation will help. Maybe but if they earn $4 in a year or so what do you pay. If they keep 5x its $20 yes. My model has quarters getting into the $1.s a few quarters out based on the current trends."
Based on Wednesday's report though my earnings model dropped further.
This stock can get into the 20s, I think with out much problem.
If demand trends pick back up they dodge the 20s but tech in general slowed meaningfully in Q3 for the first time in a few years. We also think it's slowing further in Q4, and the company expects it to slow further in Q1.
So we'd guess Micron does not dodge the 20s.
So in that time there may be many large investors who continue to ratchet down their earnings numbers which can force their price assumptions lower.
Conclusion This quarter's guide was much worse than expectations. There's no way to sugar coat it. If trends continue large investors will continue to get spooked by the drop in earnings which can further bring down the stock into the 20s.
